batch1.title: Preserve scalar choices next to MCP schema references
batch1.head: ce77eb2bb4d447657e352f9163b1dfb6bd894c30

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch1.body:
## Problem

A valid MCP input schema can narrow a reusable enum with `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Size", "enum": ["small"]}`. The converter resolves the reference first and skips the sibling `enum` or `const`. A FastMCP tool advertising only `small` consequently becomes an Atomic model that accepts and advertises `large` as well.

[JSON Schema 2020-12 permits constraints alongside `$ref`](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core#section-8.2.3.1).

## Change

Resolve scalar finite choices before a bare reference. The existing choice helper already intersects choices with the complete schema, including referenced definitions, so the generated validator and model-facing schema preserve the narrowed set without adding another validation path. Ordinary references keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

- New regression suite: **21 failures and 1 passing control on unchanged main**, then **22 passed** with the fix.
- The tests obtain real FastMCP-generated enum schemas and check both Pydantic validation and emitted JSON Schema. Additional cases cover reference chains, numeric bounds, boolean/number distinctions, nullable values, nested objects/arrays/mappings, impossible intersections, optional fields, and unresolved-reference fallback.
- [Repository validation matrix](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43883622055): **all three jobs pass**. Both the locked and lowest-direct-dependency environments pass **1,395 tests, with 14 existing skips**; the clean wheel installation and subpackage import checks pass.
- Repository-wide Black and Flake8, the AgentConfig Pyright check, and `git diff --check` pass.

The tests run locally against the installed MCP SDK, Pydantic, and JSON Schema validators; no external model calls are made.

batch2.title: Preserve article headings and attribution during webpage extraction
batch2.head: 86d283f65df1ace41cf3b87cd0338e3f50e20a10

validation_jobs.name: Real parser regressions before and after
Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch2.body:
## Problem

Both webpage scrapers delete every `header` and `footer` before selecting the main content. These elements also belong inside articles and sections, where they hold the article heading, author, publication date, or attribution. That text disappears from the Markdown returned to the agent.

The HTML standard describes these [section-scoped headers](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-header-element) and [footers](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-footer-element).

## Change

Preserve the contents of headers and footers within `main`, `article`, or `section` in both the Forge tool and the deep-research copy. Unwrap their containers so an `id="content"` or `class="main"` on a header/footer cannot become the entire main-content selection. Continue removing site-level headers/footers, navigation, scripts, and styles.

## Validation

- New regression cases on unchanged main: **8 failed, 4 passed**. All **12 pass** with the fix; the complete scraper suite passes **29 tests**.
- The tests exercise both implementations through real BeautifulSoup, readability, and Markdown conversion, with deterministic HTML fixtures supplied at the HTTP boundary. They cover article/main/section scopes, nested headings, attribution, misleading header/footer IDs/classes, and site-chrome controls.
- Live smoke test: fetched the [WordPress 6.7 release article](https://wordpress.org/news/2024/11/rollins/) successfully (HTTP 200) and processed the same response before and after the fix. The article heading and publication byline are recovered; Markdown headings increase from 16 to 17.
- [Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43885356306): all four jobs pass, including the original-source failure check, complete scraper suite, clean wheel installation, and repository quality matrix. Locked and lowest-direct-dependency environments each pass **1,373 core tests, with 14 existing skips**.
- Repository-wide Black, Flake8, the AgentConfig Pyright check, and `git diff --check` pass.

batch3.title: Preserve literal metadata field names in Qdrant filters
batch3.head: fd28bbf1b4320a570a63b0851e1644c4617ba04e

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency
Native Qdrant 1.16.0 regressions before and after
Native Qdrant 1.15.1 regressions before and after

batch3.body:
## Problem

The RAG chatbot stores metadata as a dictionary, but its Qdrant adapter inserts each metadata key directly into a JSON filter path. A stored key such as `file.name` is then interpreted as two nested keys, and `tags[0]` is interpreted as an array access. Filters can therefore return no documents even immediately after successfully inserting the matching document. Spaces and empty keys can also cause invalid-path errors.

## Changes

Quote the metadata key as one Qdrant path segment, preserving its original spelling in storage and returned results. Keep multiple predicates combined with AND and leave unfiltered queries unchanged.

Reject double quotes and backslashes with a clear `ValueError`: Qdrant's [quoted-key grammar](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/blob/222b2e44ab1c3f17e8246396ead6558e45041df7/lib/segment/src/json_path/parse.rs) does not provide an escape syntax for these characters. This avoids turning a key into additional path segments.

## Validation

The regression tests create actual local Qdrant collections, insert documents through `QdrantDBService`, and query through its public API. The OpenAI SDK uses an HTTPX transport returning deterministic embedding responses; no external model is called.

- **Qdrant client 1.15.1 and 1.16.0:** unchanged source fails **6** regressions and passes **7** controls; the fix passes all **13** on each version.
- Coverage includes dots, brackets, spaces, Unicode and empty keys, multi-predicate filtering, unchanged stored metadata, ordinary keys, unfiltered queries and unrepresentable-key rejection.
- Full core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** with both the locked and lowest direct dependencies.
- Repository Black and Flake8 checks, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43886991203) retains the before/after executions and the repository's existing quality, minimum-dependency and fresh-install jobs.

batch4.title: Preserve DSPy prediction fields across bridge operations
batch4.head: 758a7dc85dfcf2db32e1546a33ae76199c8c8c83

initial_validation.dspy_2_5_0: dependency resolution failed: historical release is published as dspy-ai, not dspy

validation_jobs.name: Native DSPy 2.5.0 pipeline before and after
Native DSPy 3.0.4 pipeline before and after
Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch4.body:
## Problem

`DSPyAtomicPipeline` uses `dir(prediction)` to collect the next stage's inputs. DSPy keeps prediction fields in its mapping, so those fields are absent from `dir()`. The current code forwards the internal `completions` property instead, and an ordinary two-stage pipeline fails with missing inputs or an unexpected `completions` argument.

## Change

Build the next input dictionary from `Prediction.items()`. This uses DSPy's public field interface, preserves the actual values and their types, and excludes internal `dspy_` fields. Each stage still receives the immediately preceding prediction, and the returned result mapping retains the original prediction objects.

## Validation

- **DSPy 3.0.4** (the lockfile version) and the historical **DSPy 2.5.0** distribution (`dspy-ai`): unchanged source fails **7** regressions and passes **2** controls; all **9** pass with the fix on both versions.
- Tests exercise real `dspy.Module` and `Prediction` objects, two- and three-stage handoffs, zero/false/null/empty values, nested Pydantic values, field names that collide with object attributes, and empty/single-stage controls.
- A two-stage `DSPyAtomicModule` test uses native predictors and DSPy's deterministic test LM, verifying that the first answer reaches the second model request. No external model call is made.
- Full core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** with both locked and lowest direct dependencies. Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43889137569) records the native before/after tests and the repository's existing checks.

## Follow-up: validated prediction fields

The same data-versus-attribute distinction also affects `run_validated()`. Prediction fields named `items`, `keys`, `get` or `completions` can resolve to SDK methods/properties instead of their values. A missing optional `items` field can likewise pick up the SDK method instead of using the schema's default.

Use the prediction's data mapping at this boundary too, selecting only fields declared by the output schema. Keep the existing Pydantic validation and defaults.

Seven additional cases report **5 failed, 2 passed** against the previous PR head. Both native DSPy **3.0.4** and **2.5.0** now pass all **16** bridge tests, including the original nine. The [follow-up validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43905894082) also passes all three repository checks: complete core suites are **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** on locked and lowest-direct dependencies. No model-service requests are made.

batch5.title: Preserve nullable and union fields in DSPy signatures
batch5.head: 995b7b0a6a2e81ba4ee0c73cc0ce6f7dd4ef1095

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency
Native DSPy 3.0.4 unions before and after
Native DSPy 2.5.0 unions before and after

batch5.body:
## Problem

The schema bridge changes the meaning of nullable and union annotations. `Optional[int]` falls back to `str`, so a numeric answer becomes a string and a null answer becomes text. The `int | None` spelling loses its null branch, while mixed unions can fail with DSPy's older signature builder. `run_validated()` then rejects an otherwise valid nullable response.

## Change

Recognize both `typing.Union` and `types.UnionType`, preserving every member, including `None`. Use a `typing.Union` annotation for compatibility with the older signature builder. Existing recursive list conversion also preserves nullable list elements.

## Validation

- Native **DSPy 3.0.4**: unchanged source fails **15** regressions and passes **2** controls; the fix passes all **17**.
- Historical **DSPy 2.5.0** (`dspy-ai`): unchanged source fails **16** regressions and passes **1** control; the fix passes all **17**.
- Tests use real DSPy signatures, predictors and the typed chat adapter with a deterministic local LM. They check advertised schemas and returned Python values for both union spellings, nulls, numbers, booleans, strings, nullable lists, nested optional values and literals, including `run_validated()`.
- Full core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** with both locked and lowest direct dependencies. Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43890073537) records the native before/after tests and the repository's existing checks.

batch6.title: Reject overlapping DSPy input and output fields
batch6.head: 04fd970bef46dd10244aaa408db1b150581c5756

validation_jobs.name: Native DSPy 3.0.4 field collisions before and after
Native DSPy 2.5.0 field collisions before and after
Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch6.body:
## Problem

DSPy stores input and output fields in one flat namespace. When the two Pydantic schemas share a field name, signature creation silently replaces the input with the output. Training-example creation also replaces the original input with the expected answer, then marks that answer as an input. For a `text -> text` task, the resulting example has the target text in `inputs()` and no target in `labels()`.

## Change

Validate that the input and output schemas have distinct Python field names before creating either a signature or a training example. Raise a clear `ValueError` listing the overlapping names. `DSPyAtomicModule` receives the same validation through signature construction. Document the requirement and a `text -> rewritten_text` example.

The check uses Python field names, so distinct fields may still share a Pydantic wire alias.

## Validation

- Native **DSPy 3.0.4** and historical **DSPy 2.5.0** (`dspy-ai`): unchanged source fails **7** regression cases and passes **2** controls; all **9** pass after the change on both versions.
- Tests cover signature, module and training-example entry points, single and multiple overlaps, defaulted fields, ordinary distinct names and matching aliases with distinct Python field names. Controls check real DSPy `input_fields`, `output_fields`, `inputs()` and `labels()`.
- Full core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** with both locked and lowest direct dependencies. Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43891613069) records native before/after tests and the repository's existing checks.

batch7.title: Honor configured caption languages in YouTube examples
batch7.head: dc342d4bb1b788bb84ce4caf72b2561ac5dc527a

validation_jobs.name: Native YouTube Transcript API 1.2.3 language selection
Native YouTube Transcript API 1.1.1 language selection
Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch7.body:
## Problem

Both YouTube example tools expose a `languages` configuration and copy it onto the tool, but never pass it to the transcript client. When the request omits `language`, the client only tries its default `en`. A configured German transcript fails to load, a German-first list can select English instead, and even the examples' default `en-US`/`en-GB` fallbacks are ignored.

## Change

Pass the existing configured list to `YouTubeTranscriptApi.fetch()` when no per-request language is supplied. An explicit request language retains its existing override behavior. Apply the same two-line fix to the summarizer and recipe examples, and document their language policy.

## Validation

- **youtube-transcript-api 1.2.3** (lockfile) and **1.1.1** (declared minimum): unchanged tools fail **8** regressions and pass **4** controls; the fix passes all **12** on each version.
- The tests run the real transcript SDK and Requests transport over deterministic page, player and caption HTTP responses. They verify the selected caption text, priority order, unavailable-language fallback, regional-English defaults, explicit overrides and unchanged configuration lists.
- Metadata lookup is supplied locally; no live YouTube request or model request is made.
- Full core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** with both locked and lowest direct dependencies. Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43892509518) records native before/after behavior and the repository's existing checks.

batch8.title: Honor Pydantic JSON number policies in tool messages
batch8.head: d72fa65c9072f4a5ac668a9fe87f9cbba862986e

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch8.body:
## Problem

`format_tool_message()` dumps Pydantic values in JSON mode, then uses the standard-library JSON encoder. JSON-mode Python values still contain non-finite floats, so the final encoder ignores Pydantic's `ser_json_inf_nan` setting. For example, a model configured for `"strings"` emits bare `Infinity` instead of `"Infinity"`, while the default `"null"` policy also emits bare constants. Those outputs are rejected by strict JSON consumers.

## Change

Use the model's JSON serialization before applying the existing spacing and ASCII escaping. This honors the number policy on root and nested models, including values produced by JSON-only field serializers. Explicit `"constants"` behavior remains supported.

This follows Pydantic's [documented number-encoding policies](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/config/#pydantic.config.ConfigDict.ser_json_inf_nan).

## Validation

- **18 new cases** cover NaN, positive/negative infinity under default, null, strings and constants policies; finite-value/Unicode formatting; nested models with differing policies; and a JSON-only serializer.
- On both locked **Pydantic 2.12.4** and the repository's lowest-direct resolution (**2.11.4**), unchanged source fails **11** cases and passes **7** controls. All new cases pass after the change.
- Existing exact-format assertions, IDs, schema-derived function names, date/UUID/Decimal/Path/Enum values and JSON field serializers remain passing.
- Full core suite: **1,391 passed, 14 skipped** in both dependency sets. The formatter has **100% coverage**. Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [three-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43894019302) records before/after results in each dependency set. No model API requests are made.

batch9.title: Keep hook registration failures from corrupting agent state
batch9.head: e784ee7660b40c5ec8c86bfcf7003cd0ededfb60

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

superseded_validation.reason: Baseline was missing from shallow checkout; validation-only fetch corrected.

batch9.body:
## Problem

A failed `register_hook()` call still appends the rejected handler to the agent's registry. With a real Instructor client, an unknown event therefore poisons later lifecycle operations: `disable_hooks()` raises before detaching normal callbacks while already reporting that hooks are disabled.

Deferred registrations have a related failure path. If `enable_hooks()` encounters an invalid event, it leaves the agent marked enabled and keeps any callbacks attached earlier in that attempt.

## Change

Retain enabled registrations only after Instructor accepts them. During resume, mark the agent enabled only after all registrations succeed; on failure, remove callbacks attached by that attempt and preserve the disabled state. The invalid deferred registration can then be removed before retrying.

Local token events, duplicate registrations, the client's event validation and callbacks owned directly by the client retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

- Six new cases use native synchronous and asynchronous Instructor hook registries, with the rejected event both before and after valid registrations.
- Unchanged main: **6 failed, 22 passed**. Fixed hook suite: **28 passed**. The cases verify rollback of duplicate callbacks, preservation of foreign callbacks, local-event suspension and successful recovery.
- Full core suite: **1,379 passed, 14 skipped** on both locked and lowest-direct dependencies; the `AtomicAgent` module has **100% coverage** in the coverage run.
- Repository-wide Black and Flake8, constructor typing, wheel installation and native Instructor/OpenAI import smoke checks pass.

The [three-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43897473312) records unchanged-source failures and repaired full-suite results in both dependency sets. No model API requests are made.

batch10.title: Isolate review contexts in the DSPy benchmark
batch10.head: 00636230a0adb349147e4951538f52c9e3486837

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch10.body:
## Problem

Stage 2 reuses a conversational agent across independent test reviews. Each request includes every earlier review and generated answer, unlike the independent predictions in the DSPy stages. This changes the evaluation context and makes request size grow throughout the benchmark. Failed requests leave their review in the next request as well.

## Change

Restore the agent's configured initial history before each review. Any intentional initial examples are retained, while earlier test predictions and failed inputs are excluded. Document the evaluation behavior and identify the guide's existing accuracy figures as results from earlier runs.

## Validation

- Four tests exercise the real Instructor and OpenAI SDK request path through an in-memory HTTP transport.
- The unchanged 30-review evaluation sends **930 message objects** across its requests, with per-request counts growing from 2 to 60. The repaired evaluation sends **60**, with 2 messages per request. These are serialized request message counts, not a token or accuracy estimate.
- Configured initial examples remain present for every review; a failed review is isolated from the next one; the single-review prediction remains unchanged.
- On both native DSPy **3.0.4** and **2.5.0**, unchanged source reports **3 failed, 1 passed**; the repaired suite reports **4 passed**.
- Complete core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** on locked and lowest-direct dependencies. Repository-wide Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43899043050) contains both unchanged-source reproductions and repaired results. Responses are deterministic offline fixtures; no model requests or new accuracy measurements were made.

batch11.title: Restore chat history after SQLite write failures
batch11.head: f27b860ba4bb3254fda864f637dce4bdee7bf635

dedupe.distinction: Prior proposal persists deletions and explicitly excludes database write failure rollback.

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch11.body:
## Problem

The SQLite history example changes its in-memory messages before persistence succeeds. A locked database can therefore reject a write or commit while leaving the new message in memory. With a capacity limit, an existing saved message has already been evicted as well. The active conversation then differs from the history restored from disk, and retrying can duplicate an unsaved append.

## Change

Snapshot the message references and turn ID before appending, and restore them if persistence raises. Restore the existing list in place so existing message/list references remain valid. Serialize writes on one instance so concurrent failures cannot restore each other's unsaved messages.

The database exception still reaches the caller. Successful writes retain the existing full-history storage format.

## Validation

Seven tests use real SQLite databases and transactions:

- An immediate write lock rejects the insert; a separate reader lock allows the insert but rejects the commit. Native statement tracing verifies that distinction.
- Both failure paths preserve unlimited and capacity-limited histories, including evicted message objects and list identity.
- A first failed write leaves no phantom turn; concurrent failures preserve the saved state.
- Retrying after releasing the lock persists the message once. Successful writes remain isolated by session.

On both locked and lowest-direct dependencies, unchanged source reports **6 failed, 1 passed**; the repaired suite reports **7 passed**. Complete core suites report **1,373 passed, 14 skipped**. Repository-wide Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [three-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43900276824) records both failure reproductions and repaired results. The SQLite busy timeout is shortened in tests; database operations and lock errors are native. No model requests are made.

dedupe.symbol_history_checked: TRAINING_DATASET across all refs including former filenames

batch12.title: Keep all genres in limited DSPy training sets
batch12.head: 57bcd8cc644f3642671f0aa41b519d1fb3e983b5

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch12.body:
## Problem

The training catalog groups ten examples of each genre together. Stage 1 takes its first 30 examples, so its optimizer never receives horror, sci-fi or romance. Stage 3 takes the first 40 and still omits sci-fi and romance, despite evaluating a six-genre classification task.

## Change

Interleave the genre groups deterministically before the existing stages select their prefixes. All 60 original examples remain present without copying or modifying their content:

- Stage 1 receives five examples of each of the six genres.
- Stage 3 receives six or seven examples per genre.

Document these candidate-pool counts in the example guide.

## Validation

Three tests exercise the actual Stage 1 training-set construction and Stage 3 conversion into native DSPy examples. They verify input keys, valid output schemas, coverage of all six genres and preservation of every original training example.

On both native DSPy **3.0.4** and **2.5.0**, unchanged source reports **2 failed, 1 passed**; the repaired suite reports **3 passed**. The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43901938335) records the actual before/after genre counts. Complete core suites report **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** on locked and lowest-direct dependencies; repository-wide Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

Tests stop at the optimizer's compile boundary without model requests. This corrects its candidate training pool; it does not claim a measured accuracy increase or that the optimizer's final few-shot selection contains every genre.

batch13.title: Route social media searches to the correct SearXNG category
batch13.head: cb1e0292b70c62be36a084ab1fb24945c21358ce

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch13.body:
## Problem

The public input accepts `social_media`, but SearXNG's category is named `social media`. Sending the underscored name causes the server's category parser to ignore it. Result filtering also compares against the underscored name, so real social-media hits are discarded.

The same issue exists in the standalone Forge tool and its deep-research, orchestration and web-search example copies.

## Change

Translate the existing public category once before requesting and filtering results. Keep `social_media` in the public input/output schemas, so callers retain the same interface. General, news and unrestricted searches retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

- New tests cover all four distributed tools across `general`, `news`, `social_media` and `None`: **4 failed, 12 passed** on unchanged source; all **16 pass** after repair.
- Including existing standalone tests: **23 passed** on locked and lowest-direct dependencies.
- Native SearXNG [`parse_generic`](https://github.com/searxng/searxng/blob/2d500cb6b8e98b5f57fb446786e91f8de03be89f/searx/webadapter.py) and `Preferences` are exercised through real local HTTP requests, with an offline engine catalog and deterministic response fixtures. Before repair, all four social searches select `general` and return no results. After repair, all select `social media` and retain the matching result; all 12 controls also pass.
- Complete core suites: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** on both dependency sets. Repository-wide Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass.

The [four-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43904001676) records unchanged-source and repaired native behavior. The current pytest-asyncio check explicitly selects function scope because the tool's existing INI file quotes that value. No live search-provider or model requests are needed.

batch14.title: Keep canonical field names in the DSPy schema bridge
batch14.head: 0da719b84ca1df273f7762e62e19d8832c94f459

validation_jobs.name: Tests on the lowest allowed version of every direct dependency

batch14.body:
## Problem

DSPy signatures use Pydantic field names, but the bridge validates those names through aliases and serializes models using their default alias policy. This breaks otherwise valid schemas:

- A canonical DSPy input is rejected when its field has a validation alias.
- A prediction cannot become the output model when that model expects an alias.
- With `serialize_by_alias=True`, training examples can lose their marked inputs or expose the wrong output labels.
- An output alias that matches another field can consume the wrong prediction value.

## Change

Accept field names alongside configured aliases when validating incoming inputs. Serialize predictor inputs and training examples with canonical field names. Validate the known canonical prediction dictionary by field name only, so external aliases cannot redirect values between output fields.

The original schemas retain their external alias policies and normal validators.

## Validation

Fourteen cases use native DSPy predictors, predictions, examples and the SDK's offline language-model fixture. Coverage includes ordinary aliases, `AliasChoices`, `AliasPath`, serialization aliases, cross-field alias collisions, explicitly aliased external inputs, normal schemas and invalid-output rejection.

On both DSPy **3.0.4** and **2.5.0**, unchanged source reports **11 failed, 3 passed**; the repaired suite reports **14 passed**. Tests also inspect the serialized predictor request to verify that the input value reaches the model adapter.

The [five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43905487124) records both reproductions and repaired results. Complete core suites report **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** on locked and lowest-direct dependencies. Repository-wide Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh-install checks pass. Responses are deterministic offline fixtures; no model-service requests are made.

batch15.title: Reject pipeline step names that overwrite stages
batch15.body:
## Problem

Pipeline stages are stored as attributes while `step_names` records their execution order. Reusing a stage name overwrites the first module but keeps both entries in the list: a two-stage pipeline silently invokes the second module twice. A stage named `forward`, `step_names`, or `predictors` can also replace a framework attribute.

## Changes

Reject names already present on the pipeline before registering the stage. Distinct names retain their order, and explicitly reusing one module under different names remains supported. Document the naming requirement.

## Validation

- Tested real DSPy modules on DSPy 3.0.4 and 2.5.0. On each version, the new regression suite produces **4 failures and 4 passing controls** against unchanged main, then **8 passing tests** with this change.
- Controls exercise ordered execution, intentional module reuse, single-stage and empty pipelines.
- Complete core suite: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** with both the locked dependencies and the lowest allowed direct dependencies.
- Black, Flake8, constructor typing, clean-wheel imports and native tracing checks pass.
- [Five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43906577392).

The native pipeline tests use deterministic local modules and require no model calls.
batch15.head: b868f00286f84d2cfde8cde1fb4add7814f50dcf

batch16.head: c6c1a466ac0ea461afd5285198e5e7d1c8db7f73
batch16.title: Honor OpenTelemetry SDK instrumentation suppression
batch16.body:
## Problem

Atomic Agents checks only the legacy string `suppress_instrumentation`. OpenTelemetry's SDK uses its generated context key when exporting spans, so an instrumented tool invoked inside an exporter still creates another span. The same mismatch affects agent calls, Instructor attempt accounting, and opt-in message capture.

A real `SimpleSpanProcessor` reproduces the problem: exporting one outer span invokes a local tool while the SDK suppression flag is true, yet the tool creates a second exported span.

## Changes

Recognize the SDK key as well as the existing legacy flag across agent/tool tracing, attempt hooks, and message capture. Suppressed operations still execute normally. Keep message-content access behind the suppression check, and resume normal tracing when the context ends.

This matches the SDK's [exporter suppression context](https://opentelemetry-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_modules/opentelemetry/sdk/trace/export.html).

## Validation

- OpenTelemetry API/SDK **1.30.0 and 1.38.0**: **9 failures and 8 passing controls** against unchanged main, then **17 passing tests** on each version.
- Coverage includes a real SDK exporter invoking a real tool, sync/async agent calls, both streaming paths, threaded tools, delayed response/error hooks, message access, and legacy-key compatibility.
- Complete core suite: **1,382 passed, 14 skipped** with both locked dependencies and the lowest allowed direct dependencies.
- Black, Flake8, constructor typing, fresh-wheel imports and native tracing checks pass.
- [Five-job validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43908869835).

No new runtime dependency is added.

batch17.title: Resolve literal names in MCP resource URI templates
batch17.body:
## Problem

The MCP resource discovery path accepts literal URI-template variables such as `{item.name}`, `{0}`, and `{01}`, but the generated resource uses Python's `str.format` to expand them. Python interprets these as attribute access or positional arguments. Expansion then falls back to the original template, so a valid resource input reaches the MCP server with an unexpanded address and fails to read the resource.

## Change

Look up each variable name literally when formatting resource URIs, for both fresh and persistent sessions. This extends the existing simple-template subset to valid dotted and numeric variable names; it does not add URI-template operators or change value escaping.

This is outside the intentionally limited expansion scope documented in #345 and is separate from the argument-encoding changes in #373, which retain Python field-name lookup. RFC 6570 section 2.3 permits these variable names: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570#section-2.3

Two existing assertions characterized the old dotted-name fallback. They now assert successful expansion, and separate malformed-template cases retain coverage for the existing fallback behavior.

## Validation

- Native MCP ClientSession and low-level Server communicate through JSON-round-tripped in-memory transports. Real resource listing, generated input validation, resource reads, and session reuse are covered.
- MCP SDK 1.8.0 and 1.22.0: **8 failed / 6 passed on unchanged main → 14 passed with the change**. Controls cover ordinary names, repeated variables, encoded names and literal URI paths, plus malformed-template fallback for both session modes.
- Full core suite with locked dependencies and minimum direct dependencies: **1,385 passed, 14 skipped** in each environment.
- Black, Flake8, constructor typing, and clean-wheel import checks passed.

batch18.body: ## Problem Both webpage scrapers select the first matching content element even when it is empty. An accessibility target such as `` can therefore win over the article and make a successful scrape return only a newline. Empty placeholders also hide later candidates of the same kind. This layout occurs in the [Drupal Bootstrap page template](https://git.drupalcode.org/project/bootstrap/-/blob/8.x-3.x/templates/system/page.html.twig), which places the empty target before the page content inside a `div.main-container`. ## Change Continue through candidates in the existing priority order until one contains text or media. Preserve image-only and other media-only candidates, including media elements that carry the matching ID themselves. Keep the body fallback when every candidate is empty. Apply the same fix to the Forge scraper and the deep-research copy. This is independent of #442's header/footer preservation: that patch still fails the same 12 new article-selection regressions. ## Validation - Real Requests HTTP calls, BeautifulSoup, readability, and Markdownify exercise both public scraper entry points. - On unchanged main, and separately with #442 applied: **12 failed, 24 passed**. The failures cover empty skip targets, whitespace/comments, later ID/class/main/article matches, and the body fallback. - After the change: **53 passed**, including the existing scraper suite. Controls retain candidate priority and image/audio/video/iframe/object/embed/SVG/canvas selection. - Repeated with locked parser versions and their minimum compatible versions: **53 passed** in both environments. - Full core suite with locked and minimum direct dependencies: **1,373 passed, 14 skipped** in each environment. - Black, Flake8, constructor typing, and clean-wheel import checks passed. batch19.title: Include the durable research plan in shared agent context
batch19.body:
## Problem

`ResearchStateProvider` is documented to expose the current plan, sources, and learnings to the shared agent prompts, but it never reads `ResearchState.plan`. A populated plan with several sub-topics still renders "No research has been done yet." until sources or learnings exist. Later prompts also omit the planned topics, their initial queries, and their current sufficiency state.

## Change

Render the durable plan before the existing sources and learnings. Preserve topic/query order and read the live `SubTopic.sufficient` flags on each call, so all generators sharing the provider see state updates. Keep the prior output byte-for-byte when the plan is empty.

The plan remains data in the existing dynamic-context section. The user's question continues through the existing input schemas.

This differs from #425, which improves learning-grouping performance while preserving the old rendered text; its implementation still fails the same plan-presence regressions.

## Validation

- Nine new cases use the actual `ResearchState`, `SubTopic`, provider, and `SystemPromptGenerator`.
- On unchanged main, and separately with #425 applied: **5 failed, 4 passed**. With this change, the new cases and existing system-prompt tests report **20 passed**.
- Cover multiple topics and queries, both status values, all source/learning combinations, shared generators after mutation, clearing the plan, and unchanged state after rendering.
- Combined core and new example tests: **1,382 passed, 14 skipped**, with both locked and minimum direct dependencies.
- Black, Flake8, constructor typing, and clean-wheel import checks passed.

Validation run: https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43918699661

batch20.difference_from_456: SDK sampling and API-only NoOp spans stay nonrecording without the suppression context. This change skips only payload work and preserves span creation and propagation; 456 instead honors a separate suppression context flag.
batch20.head: d44a6131d5095f8806b9249eb5adee80b29bbb1c
batch20.body:
## What changes

Nonrecording spans currently serialize structured tool/agent inputs and outputs and traverse opt-in chat messages before the OpenTelemetry API discards those attributes. This occurs with a real SDK `ALWAYS_OFF` sampler and with an API-only `NoOpTracerProvider`, even when instrumentation suppression is not enabled.

Check `span.is_recording()` at the two payload entry points before doing that work. Span creation, sampling inputs, context propagation, tool results and exception behavior stay intact. `RECORD_ONLY` spans still receive their payloads even though their sampled flag is unset.

## Validation

[Native SDK comparisons and full validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/atomic-agents/actions/runs/43920152252):

- OpenTelemetry SDK **1.30.0** and **1.38.0**: the 25 new cases go from **13 failed / 12 passed** on `main` to **25 passed**. They cover synchronous/asynchronous calls and exceptions, `ALWAYS_OFF`, `ALWAYS_ON`, `RECORD_ONLY`, API-only no-op spans, input/output chat capture, and valid parent/child context propagation.
- Complete core suite on both locked and lowest allowed direct dependencies: **1,398 passed, 14 skipped**.
- Black, Flake8, constructor typing and fresh wheel/import checks passed. The new guard paths are covered.

The same validation runs also measure complete instrumented `Echo.run` calls with a **1,000,000-byte** text payload, an unchanged return object, **100 calls per trial**, five warmup calls and five measured trials. These measurements isolate tracing overhead in a trivial tool:

| Native SDK | Median 100-call time before | After | Payload serializations before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1.30.0 | 95.45 ms | 1.08 ms | 200 → 0 |
| 1.38.0 | 103.79 ms | 2.02 ms | 200 → 0 |

The two `is_recording()` guards are the only production changes.
